headline: South Asia: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya.
- Africa: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
- India: Israel must prepare for another Iran war, ex-Mossad chief warns Tehran deal won't hold.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
- Military Times, one hour ago: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
Trump said he wanted to move forward with the controlled blasts but is putting the decision in the hands of the courts.
- Military Times, 5 hours ago: B-2 bomber wings awarded Presidential Unit Citation for Midnight Hammer.
The award marks the first time a bomber unit has been recognized with a President Unit Citation since the Vietnam War.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Under Hegseth, the OSS rides again — kind of.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth resurrected the OSS, created during the Second World War under "Wild Bill" Donovan.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: VFW seeks veterans’ input on health care experiences in and out of VA.
Through early January, Veterans of Foreign Wars is conducting a survey of veterans on their health care experiences, including medical treatment received at the Department of Veterans Affairs or in private care.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Robbers reach end of road with rare armoured car heist convictions.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Robbers reach end of road with rare armoured car heist convictions.
A string of robberies targeting armoured money-courier companies has yielded two convictions in two months, but the attacks continue, with the latest incident occurring in Liguanea, St Andrew, earlier this month. The two recent convictions mark the first time in 17 years that individuals have faced sentencing following successful prosecutions for offences linked to armoured-car robberies since the last such conviction in 2009.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: Generations bound by Howard.
WESTERN BUREAU: For generations, Howard University has been a home away from home for Jamaicans, where families have sent their children to acquire world-class skills, build successful careers and forge friendships that last a lifetime. From engineers and architects to doctors and lawyers, the historically Black institution in Washington, DC, has helped shape the professional journeys of Jamaicans, with some families establishing traditions that span generations.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians launch airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia: six injured – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russians launch airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia: six injured – photos.
Six people have been injured in Russian strikes on the city of Zaporizhzhia.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Germany's Merz urges Russia to stop "dangerous provocations" after missiles fall in Poland.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Russia to stop dangerous provocations after Russian missiles fell in Poland, pledging full solidarity with Warsaw.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: "A little miracle": three cats rescued at site of Russian strike in Dymer, one found completely buried – photo.
Rescue workers found a cat under the rubble of a building destroyed in a Russian attack in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast. The animal was completely buried under sand, dust and construction debris but survived. The cat was named Dym and taken to a veterinary clinic.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: NATO strengthens protection after Russian missiles violate Polish airspace.
Poland's Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz says allied aircraft will complement ground-based systems, Polish F-16s and other NATO fighter jets.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Ukraine takes the war against Russia far from its borders.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Ukraine takes the war against Russia far from its borders.
It's the first time Kyiv has admitted to striking Russian ships so far from home.
- Balkan Insight, 6 hours ago: Serbia’s Student Movement Criticises European Parliament’s Vukovar Resolution.
Student movement says draft resolution marking 35th anniversary of Croatian town's fall offers only 'one-sided interpretation of the past' and ignores Serb suffering elsewhere during the Croatia war.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Sudan: UN, U.S. Condemn Khartoum Drone Strikes - Sudan Renews Allegations of Attacks Launched From Ethiopia.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The United Nations and the United States have condemned Sunday's drone attacks in Sudan's capital, Khartoum, which damaged a civilian neighborhood and UN premises, as Sudan renewed allegations that drones used in attacks across its territory were launched from Ethiopia.
- Africanews, 9 hours ago: Libyan naval forces remain on high alert after strike on Russian vessel in Benghazi.
A military official says that naval forces in eastern Libya will remain on high alert to counter any threat after attacks targeted two vessels, including at least one Russian ship, off Benghazi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that Ukrainian forces were behind the strikes.
- Africanews, 16 hours ago: Drone strikes hit homes and UN premises in Sudan's capital.
The United Nations confirmed that one of its premises, with UN personnel inside, was damaged in the attacks. It condemned the risks posed to humanitarian workers in civilian areas.
- Africanews, 14 hours ago: UN calls for probe after drone attacks hit ships off Libya.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for either strike on Sunday off the port city of Benghazi, but they came as Ukrainian forces stepped up attacks against Russia far from the front lines.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza.
Israel continues to launch attacks across the enclave, despite an October 2025 'ceasefire' deal.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Russia threatens ‘hostile’ Estonia with ‘open war’.
Moscow accuses Tallinn of 'hostile actions' citing border closure and claiming it is allowing Ukraine to launch attacks.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Iran hits US bases and civilian sites in the Gulf after a lull.
Tehran has ramped up attacks in recent days as the US naval blockade and sanctions campaign hurt the country.
- Jerusalem Post, 3 hours ago: Iran faces growing food shortages, but regime collapse unlikely during war, expert warns.
The country has managed to overcome the killing of Khamenei, but questions remain over what form the regime will take, particularly whether it will become more military-oriented or more religious.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Bullets Beat Wanderers 2-1 As Chaomba Strikes Late.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 hours ago: Malawi: Bullets Beat Wanderers 2-1 As Chaomba Strikes Late.
[Nyasa Times] FCB Nyasa Big Bullets have claimed the bragging rights in the Blantyre derby after a dramatic 2-1 win over Mighty Wanderers, with George Chaomba scoring the winner deep into added time.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 2 hours ago: Malawi: Mphepo Honoured for 50 Years of Humanitarian Service.
[Nyasa Times] Malawian humanitarian worker Lion Francis Mphepo has received the International President's Award from Lions Clubs International, in recognition of five decades of service to marginalised people around the world.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: South Africa: Is South Africa Losing Ground Against HIV? These Four Graphs Offer a Warning.
[Bhekisisa] Findings from one of the world's largest ongoing population surveys tracking HIV, in rural KwaZulu-Natal, are "a sobering warning", researchers say. All four indicators they analysed show that the momentum in bringing the HIV epidemic under control has been lost -- which could mean it could start growing again. It's a pivotal moment, experts say. South Africa will have to get smart about testing people and getting them on to treatment or prevention if the country were to end HIV as a public health

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, AllAfrica - Conflict, Ukrainska Pravda, Times of India - Top Stories, The Moscow Times, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya.
President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines. But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”. “It all took place off the coast of Libya.
- The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: 17 killed in Saudi attack on Yemeni city: Houthis.
Coalition airstrikes on telecoms facilities killed 17 workers, wounded 11 more, and caused the “total destruction” of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other sites, the Houthis’ Telecommunications Ministry said
- The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran.
War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Analysis: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel.
The International Court of Justice’s landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa’s genocide case against Israel over the war on Gaza, legal experts said, establishing a precedent that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective. While the conflicts in Gaza and Myanmar are legally distinct, both cases before the World Court are based on allegations that states breached their obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention.
India - bottom line: Israel must prepare for another Iran war, ex-Mossad chief warns Tehran deal won't hold.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Israel must prepare for another Iran war, ex-Mossad chief warns Tehran deal won't hold.
As Israel contemplates military action against Iran amid escalating tensions, former Mossad chief David Barnea proposes war as a means to destabilize Iran's regime. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for US backing on immediate strikes, but faces resistance from Gadi Eisenkot. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump is advocating for diplomacy and economic measures rather than military intervention, highlighting a stark strategic disconnect between Israeli and American leadership.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Kaliningrad's $576m lifeline, Russia plans ferries to bypass Europe restrictions.
Russia is set to allocate $576 million towards the construction of two railway ferries intended to bolster supply routes to Kaliningrad. Announced by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, the ferries are expected to be operational by 2030. This initiative will strengthen maritime transport and diminish reliance on overland pathways through Lithuania amid ongoing tensions. Given Kaliningrad's strategic location, these ferries are crucial for enhancing Russia's military logistics in the region.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 10 hours ago: Delhi man stabs 5 policemen inside police station, shot at in encounter after escape.
Nabeel was summoned to Jama Masjid police station over a family dispute involving his mother and sister. During questioning, he allegedly attacked police personnel with a knife, injuring nine of them. He then fled the station and allegedly robbed a commuter of his two-wheeler at knifepoint. A police team tracked him to the Chitli Qabar area, where he allegedly resisted apprehension and was shot in an encounter.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 11 hours ago: China-to-B'desh cargo ship seized: Chemicals onboard enough to make 100 missiles.
The Indonesian Navy detained the MV Star Line cargo vessel off Belawan while it was en route from China to Bangladesh. It was found carrying 405 tonnes of sodium perchlorate, a powerful oxidising agent used in explosives. Additionally, the vessel contained millions of unregistered 4G LTE SIM cards, raising further concerns. Investigations revealed inconsistencies in the ship’s registration documents and cargo specifics.
Asia - bottom line: How will China’s ties with Myanmar change with the ICJ’s genocide ruling?.
- South China Morning Post - China, 14 hours ago: How will China’s ties with Myanmar change with the ICJ’s genocide ruling?.
An international court ruling of genocide against Myanmar might complicate Beijing’s diplomatic engagement with Naypyidaw and cast a shadow over Belt and Road Initiative infrastructure projects in the country, observers warn. The landmark decision by the UN’s highest judicial body covers Myanmar’s 2017 military campaign against the majority-Muslim Rohingya minority in Rakhine state that killed at least 10,000 people and forced hundreds of thousands more to flee. The decision handed down on...
- Taipei Times, just now: Finnish parliament warms to hardening border with Russia.
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: EU moves to ban Russian flags at sports events under new sanctions.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has announced a proposal for the next sanctions package over Russia’s war against Ukraine that would ban Russian teams and individual athletes from competing under the Russian flag at events in the EU in the future. The plan also includes banning the display of official Russian symbols and restricting financial flows from Russian sponsors to sports and cultural associations based in Europe. Russian nationals would also no longer be allowed to...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Armenian PM unveils draft constitution, key to Azerbaijan peace deal.
Armenian leader Nikol Pashinyan unveiled a proposed new constitution on Monday that would get rid of a claim to the Karabakh region, saying it was the only way to reach a peace deal with Azerbaijan. The Caucasus foes spent three decades locked in a territorial conflict over the mountainous region following the fall of the Soviet Union. In a 2023 offensive, Baku retook the Armenian-populated region, forcing a mass exodus. It has since demanded Yerevan remove claims to Karabakh from its...

- NK News, 14 hours ago: US senator warns North Korea growing ‘more lethal’ due to Ukraine war.
North Korea’s deployment of troops to support Russia’s war against Ukraine is turning the country into a more capable military threat, a prominent U.S. senator has warned, arguing that this will constrain Washington’s freedom to act. Speaking at the Halifax International Security Forum over the weekend, Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware said cooperation among […]

SEOUL, Nov. 24 (Yonhap) -- A Seoul court on Tuesday issued an arrest warrant for...

SEOUL, Nov. 23 (Yonhap) -- South Korea will offer rewards of up to 500 million w...
- Yonhap News Agency, 16 hours ago: Court holds arrest warrant hearings for 8 election officials.
SEOUL, Nov. 23 (Yonhap) -- A court on Monday held arrest warrant hearings for ei...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Legal battle looms over potential Russian return to international sport.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: Legal battle looms over potential Russian return to international sport.
The IOC is pushing for Russia to return to Olympic competition after years of exclusion due to the war in Ukraine but a legal quagmire looms ahead of growing opposition to a potential comeback.
- ABC News Australia, 2 hours ago: W Award winner Georgie 'not anymore' in older sister Maddy's shadow.
Six years after COVID-19 disruptions saw Georgie Prespakis present the W Award to Maddy in their backyard, she lifts her own to make them the first sisters to win AFLW's best and fairest.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: ACT government given 12 months to review 'offensive' Indigenous protocol.
The ACT government has been given 12 months to deliver a review of how it acknowledges First Nations people.
